QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_50

question.text: Arjun invested Rs.8,00,000 in a fund that grew to Rs.11,20,000 over 3 years. He also received Rs.24,000 in dividends, which for this calculation are simply added to the ending value (dividend timing is ignored). Which option is the CLOSEST approximation of the total return CAGR?

explanation.text: The Logic: Total ending value including dividends = Rs.11,20,000 + Rs.24,000 = Rs.11,44,000. Using the workbook's CAGR formula, CAGR = ((End value / Beginning value)^(1/n)) - 1 = ((11,44,000 / 8,00,000)^(1/3)) - 1, which is approximately 12.64%. Of the choices given, 13.00% is the closest approximation. The Trap: Using only the ending NAV of Rs.11,20,000 (ignoring dividends) gives roughly 11.87%; 40% is the simple non-annualized total return; 14.33% does not match this calculation. Note: The workbook also defines total return as periodic income plus capital gain, which is why dividends are added to the ending value before computing CAGR. If dividend timing mattered exactly, XIRR with cash-flow dates would be the appropriate tool.
